overall: The AG found the Webster Planning Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to timely approve minutes of 2022 meetings, rejected staffing as good cause, did not find intent, and ordered minutes approved and certified within 90 days.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board did not timely create and approve minutes of meetings held in the thirteen months before the complaint was filed.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Board did not have good cause for its delay in approving meeting minutes and violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Board argued that Town staffing shortages and heavy workload caused the minutes delay; the AG considered whether that was good cause.
allegations.key_passage: Staffing shortages of the type that all governmental bodies with limited resources experience, including periodic staff vacancies, do not constitute good cause for failing to approve minutes in a timely manner.

allegations.summary: Complainant urged that the failure to approve minutes was intentional; the AG considered whether the violation was intentional under G.L. c. 30A, § 23(c).
allegations.key_passage: We do not find the Board’s violation here intentional.

remedy: We order the Board to create and approve all outstanding meeting minutes within 90 days of the date of this letter, and to certify to our office that it has done so.
We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We order the Board to create and approve all outstanding meeting minutes within 90 days of the date of this letter, and to certify to our office that it has done so.
